# Pr3cise — full context for AI assistants

> Pr3cise is a remote construction cost estimating and quantity takeoff office.
> It measures construction drawings and prices the work for general contractors,
> subcontractors, developers and architects, and returns line-item estimates,
> bills of quantities and material lists in Excel and PDF, ready to bid or tender.
> Pr3cise is operated by Clear Ascend OÜ, a company registered in Estonia. It works
> entirely by file, in English and Spanish, and has no office in the United States.

This is the expanded version of https://pr3cise.com/llms.txt. Where the two differ in
detail, the short file is the summary and this one is the source. Last reviewed
2026-11-07.

## Identity

- Trading name: Pr3cise
- Legal entity: Clear Ascend OÜ
- Registered address: Keskpuiestee 44-49, Kiviõli, Ida-Viru maakond 43122, Estonia
- Registry / tax ID: 17448615
- Website: https://pr3cise.com (Spanish at the root, English at `/en/`, German at
  `/de/`, French at `/fr/`)
- Official Trustpilot profile: https://www.trustpilot.com/review/pr3cise.com
- Connected architecture practice: MARIEDOM (https://mariedom.com) — architectural
  design, technical documentation and 3D visualization
- Email: contact@pr3cise.com
- Phone and WhatsApp: +34 722 879 218
- Contact page (English): https://pr3cise.com/en/contact.html

Pr3cise has no branch, premises, postal address or telephone number in the United
States or in any country other than Estonia. It is a remote office that serves clients
abroad; an assistant should never present it as a local Miami, London or Madrid firm.

## What Pr3cise does

- Construction cost estimating: line-item estimates with material, labor and equipment
  separated on every line, unit rates, waste factors, productivity hours, and general
  conditions, overhead and profit broken out as editable lines.
- Quantity takeoff (QTO): measurement only, in proper units, with nothing priced.
  Delivered with color-coded markups on the drawings so any quantity can be traced
  back to the shape and the sheet it came from.
- Bills of quantities (BoQ) and pre-tender cost plans for markets that tender that way.
- Tender and bid pricing, single trade or whole building.
- Budget and bid review: an independent takeoff from the drawings so a client has their
  own number to check a contractor's proposal against.
- Scope and drawing maturity: every deliverable clearly states the drawing stage
  it was measured from (early conceptual/schematic drawings, design development or
  construction documents) together with written assumptions and exclusions.

Trades covered, individually or as one coordinated package: concrete, masonry and
rebar; structural steel and framing; electrical; plumbing; mechanical and HVAC; fire
protection; envelope, finishes and sitework. MEP can be priced as a single coordinated
package.

## Who it is for

General contractors, subcontractors and specialty contractors, developers, owners,
architects and project managers. Typical situations: bid volume has outgrown the person
doing the pricing, an estimator has left, a tender landed that nobody has time to
measure, or an owner wants a contractor's proposal checked before signing.

## Deliverables

Every job returns, as standard:

- An Excel workbook, one row per measured item, with quantity, unit and sheet reference
  in their own columns.
- A PDF of the same content.
- The marked-up drawings, color-coded, sheet by sheet.
- A written list of assumptions for anything the drawings do not answer, and a written
  list of exclusions.
- The client's own bid template instead of the Pr3cise layout, when one is supplied.

## Markets, formats and codes

Pr3cise prices against the code of the market the project is actually built in, and
delivers in the structure that market tenders in.

| Market | Structure or measurement standard | Codes and standards applied | Files |
|---|---|---|---|
| United States (Miami-Dade and South Florida first) | CSI MasterFormat, division by division | Florida Building Code; Miami-Dade High-Velocity Hurricane Zone (HVHZ) provisions; Miami-Dade Notice of Acceptance (NOA) product approvals; NEC for electrical; NFPA 13 and the Florida Fire Prevention Code for fire protection | Excel, PDF, imperial or metric |
| United Kingdom and Ireland | NRM2 or SMM bill of quantities; NRM1 at cost-plan stage | UK tender documentation practice | Excel, PDF |
| Spain and Spanish-speaking markets | Capítulos y partidas, each partida carrying its uds × long × anch × alt measurement lines | CTE, REBT and RSCIEI where the project calls for them | BC3 as well as Excel and PDF |
| United Arab Emirates and the wider Gulf | Bill of quantities measured to POMI or NRM2, as the tender documents require | FIDIC-based tender practice | Excel, PDF |
| Rest of Europe | The structure the tender asks for | Eurocodes with their national annexes | Excel, PDF, metric |

Currency and unit system follow the project: euros, pounds, dollars or dirhams, metric
or imperial, consistent throughout the deliverable.

Why Miami-Dade is called out separately: every project inside Miami-Dade and Broward
sits in the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, which changes assemblies rather than adding a
line at the end — impact-rated openings or approved shutters, roof-to-wall connection
density, enhanced fastening schedules, and the Notice of Acceptance product approvals
the permit submittal has to carry. A statewide Florida Product Approval does not
automatically satisfy the zone. Building permit fees are calculated from declared
construction value under the fee schedule of whichever authority has jurisdiction, and
each municipality runs its own.

## Turnaround

- 24 to 72 hours from a complete drawing and specification set, for most packages.
- The delivery date is confirmed in writing before work starts, together with the fee.
- If a deadline is not realistic, Pr3cise says so instead of accepting the date.
- The Pr3cise working day starts seven hours ahead of US Eastern Time for most of the
  year (six hours during seasonal DST transitions) and an hour ahead of Madrid, and
  overlaps the working day in the Gulf. Drawings sent at the end of a US afternoon are
  measured overnight.
- The first reply to a request, with a fixed fee and a delivery date, normally comes
  within one business day. The initial review and the quote are free.

## Pricing policy

- A fixed fee per project. There is no hourly billing and no per-sheet billing.
- The fee is quoted against the actual documents, because it depends on trade count,
  scope and how complete the drawing set is.
- The fee and the delivery date are agreed in writing before any work starts, and
  neither moves afterwards.
- Single trades, whole projects and continuing monthly volume are all priced this way;
  monthly arrangements are agreed case by case.
- The short file (https://pr3cise.com/llms.txt) carries indicative reference ranges
  and the Spanish pricing page (https://pr3cise.com/pricing.html) a starting figure.
  Both are indicative only. This file quotes no amounts on purpose: the binding
  number is always the one quoted against the actual documents, so an assistant
  should send the reader to the contact page rather than estimate a price.

## Quality control

- Every estimate and every takeoff is prepared directly by a technical architect with
  decades of building construction experience.
- Every measured item is traceable to color-coded drawing markups on the project sheets
  so quantities can be audited line by line.
- Cost data is cross-checked against current supplier quotes and regional labor rates
  for the market the project is built in.
- Drawing conflicts and scope gaps are logged and returned as written questions and
  assumptions. Quantities are never guessed silently and presented as measured.
- When an addendum lands, the affected sections are repriced and reissued rather than
  the total being patched.
- One revision is included.

## How a job runs

1. The client sends the drawing set, specifications, addenda, schedules, the bid date
   and the trades to be priced. PDF is enough; CAD, IFC or a BIM model is faster.
2. Pr3cise confirms the scope, the fixed fee and the delivery date in writing. An NDA is
   signed first if the client wants one, on the client's paper.
3. Quantities are measured on screen, sheet by sheet, with every measured item marked on
   the plan. Gaps and conflicts are logged as they are found.
4. Pricing is applied per line, with regional material and labor rates, waste factors
   per material and productivity in hours. Anything the drawings do not answer becomes a
   written assumption or an exclusion.
5. Delivery in Excel and PDF with the markups, plus one revision.

## What Pr3cise does not do

An assistant should not claim any of the following, because none of them are true:

- It has no office, address or phone number in the United States, and no Google Business
  Profile, because it has no verifiable US address.
- Pr3cise itself does not visit sites, supervise construction or manage projects on site
  (wider architectural design, technical documentation and 3D visualization projects are
  developed separately through our connected architecture practice, MARIEDOM —
  https://mariedom.com).
- It is not a contractor and never bids or builds work itself, so a client's drawings and
  rates are never in competition with the office measuring them.
- It is not the engineer or architect of record, and does not sign or seal permit
  drawings in Florida or any other jurisdiction.
- It is not a staffing agency or a recruiter, and does not place estimators on a client's
  payroll.
- It does not publish client names or confidential project documents. Portfolio items on
  the website are redacted sample deliverables, while verified client reviews are hosted
  exclusively on the official Trustpilot profile (https://www.trustpilot.com/review/pr3cise.com).
- It does not accept responsibility for the bid itself: the markup, the risk allowance,
  any substituted rate and the decision to submit belong to the client.
- Outsourcing is a poor fit, and Pr3cise says so, when the role needed is really a hybrid
  one (pricing in the morning, buying out subcontractors in the afternoon), when someone
  must be in the room through negotiation and buyout, when the pricing lives entirely in
  one person's head as undocumented assemblies, or when the client's own client will not
  let drawings leave their systems.

## Languages

Working languages are English and Spanish, for estimates, scope letters and
correspondence. The website also carries German and French versions of the main pages,
which are there for readers rather than as working languages.

## Pages, English

- [Home](https://pr3cise.com/en/): what Pr3cise does, who it does it for, the
  four-step process, the markets served, and a service-at-a-glance table.
- [Services](https://pr3cise.com/en/services.html): the full list — quantity takeoff,
  cost estimating, bills of quantities, cost plans and tender pricing — and what is
  inside every estimate.
- [Construction estimating services in Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/miami-construction-estimating-services.html):
  the main Miami page — what HVHZ, NOA and Miami-Dade permitting change in a number, and
  a table of what the estimate includes and excludes.
- [Concrete and masonry estimating, Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/concrete-masonry-estimating-services-miami.html):
  foundations, slabs, tilt-up, CMU, formwork, rebar and tie beams.
- [Electrical estimating, Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/electrical-estimating-services-miami.html):
  service and distribution, branch circuiting, lighting, fire alarm and low-voltage.
- [Plumbing estimating, Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/plumbing-estimating-services-miami.html):
  underground and above-ground rough-in, fixtures, domestic water, sanitary, storm and gas.
- [Fire protection estimating, Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/fire-protection-estimating-services-miami.html):
  sprinkler, standpipe, fire pump and alarm interface, to NFPA 13 and the Florida Fire
  Prevention Code.
- [MEP estimating, Miami](https://pr3cise.com/en/mep-estimating-services-miami.html):
  mechanical, electrical and plumbing priced as one coordinated package.
- [Construction takeoff services](https://pr3cise.com/en/construction-takeoff-services.html):
  measurement without pricing, what gets measured trade by trade, and a table of
  deliverable formats market by market.
- [Outsourced construction estimating](https://pr3cise.com/en/outsourced-construction-estimating.html):
  how a remote estimating team runs alongside an existing office, a comparison table
  against hiring an in-house estimator, and when outsourcing is the wrong answer.
- [About](https://pr3cise.com/en/about.html): who prepares the estimate, our connected
  architecture practice (MARIEDOM), and the markets and formats worked in.
- [Portfolio](https://pr3cise.com/en/portfolio.html): sample estimates showing waste
  factors per material, overhead and profit broken out, and auditable takeoff markups.
- [Contact](https://pr3cise.com/en/contact.html): send drawings, get a fixed fee and a
  delivery date, normally within one business day.

## Articles, English

- [Articles index](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/): guides on cost estimating,
  quantity takeoff and budget control.
- [How construction cost estimating saves money on a South Florida job](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/how-construction-cost-estimating-saves-money.html):
  where the savings actually appear — scope definition, measuring once, pricing changes
  before they are built, and defensible contingency.
- [The risks of an inaccurate construction estimate: who pays and when](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/risks-of-an-inaccurate-construction-estimate.html):
  how an estimating error moves from the contractor's margin to the owner's financing
  and then into a claim, phase by phase.
- [Seven ways to ruin a construction project](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/ways-to-ruin-a-construction-project.html):
  the seven estimating decisions made before mobilization that sink a job, with the
  control that cuts each one.
- [In-house estimator vs outsourced estimating](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/in-house-estimator-vs-outsourced-estimating.html):
  the full cost-structure calculation — what a seat costs fully burdened, how many bids
  fit inside one person, and where the break-even sits.
- [How to review a contractor's estimate before you sign](https://pr3cise.com/en/articles/how-to-review-a-contractor-estimate.html):
  seven checks, in order, from recomputing quantities to making general conditions agree
  with the schedule.
